texts: mixed: the important part is right — dryness is tied to the neap-tide condition and is not asserted of tide-pools in general — but the parser also emits a taxonomy atom classifying a neap tide as "neap", which says slightly more than your sentence does. That is a translator slip rather than a wording problem: the sentence is already in the ideal shape for a conditional property, so leave it as written and have it re-parsed.

mixed: the claim itself lands correctly as a kind-level "salt-bloom needs spring-tide fills", but the parser adds an unstated taxonomy atom about spring tides, and once that atom is dropped the stacked compound "spring-tide fills" is one opaque label with nothing tying it back to spring tides — a later question about spring tides will not reach this rule. Un-stack the modifier so each piece keeps its own symbol: "Salt-bloom needs spring tides to fill the tide-pools." (that names the tide-pools as what gets filled — substitute whatever your lore has the spring tide fill).
